notes: V5 Stage 3 (Issue #16) evidence packet registry. Each packet is the deterministic boundary of what a writer may assert for its topic: approved_claim_ids is the ceiling, mandatory_claim_ids are non-negotiable, source_ids are pre-resolved so a writer never needs to query the source registry ad hoc. source_registry_revision/claim_registry_revision are sha256 hashes of the live registries at generation time (computeRegistryRevisionHash in lib/evidence-packet-registry.ts) — if either registry changes, isPacketStale() will report this packet as stale and it must be regenerated before being trusted again.

packets.canonical_question: What does a BMI number actually measure, and what are its limitations?
packets.reader_intent: Understand what a BMI number does and does not tell them about their health.
required_limitations: Does not itself quantify how large the BMI-vs-body-fat discrepancy is for any individual.
prohibited_claims: BMI is an accurate measure of body fat for every individual
BMI directly measures body fat
allowed_conclusions: BMI is a surrogate, population-level measure of body fatness and should be interpreted alongside other information.

packets.canonical_question: What happens inside the body during intermittent fasting?
packets.reader_intent: Understand the underlying mechanism of intermittent fasting before deciding whether to try it.
required_limitations: A narrative review synthesizing many underlying studies, not a single controlled trial of the mechanism itself.
Exact fasting duration needed to trigger the switch varies by individual and was not reduced to one number in this source.
prohibited_claims: the metabolic switch happens at exactly the same time for everyone
fasting immediately switches the body to ketone use
allowed_conclusions: Sufficiently long fasting periods shift the body toward ketone-based fuel use, per the cited review.
uncertainty_notes: Exact individual timing of the switch is not established by this source.

packets.canonical_question: What are the FDA-approved uses, expected results, and major safety warnings for semaglutide (Wegovy) for weight management?
packets.reader_intent: Gather baseline facts before a clinician conversation about semaglutide for weight management.
required_limitations: Trial population (STEP 1) excluded people with diabetes.
STEP 1's 68-week result does not by itself establish durability beyond the study period.
The thyroid C-cell tumor finding is from rodent studies; the label states human relevance has not been determined.

This packet's regulatory-status claim covers only the adult weight-management and cardiovascular-risk-reduction indications shared by both the injection and tablet formulations — it does not cover the injection-only pediatric (ages 12+) obesity indication or the injection-only MASH treatment indication.
required_safety_context: carries a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodent studies
is contraindicated in people with a personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2
prohibited_claims: cures obesity
guarantees weight loss
produces the same result for every person
has been proven to cause thyroid cancer in humans
approved for cosmetic weight loss with no medical indication required
approved for pediatric use or MASH treatment in tablet form
allowed_conclusions: Wegovy (semaglutide), in its injection and tablet formulations, is FDA-approved for weight management under specific conditions and produced substantially greater weight loss than placebo in its pivotal trial.
The injection formulation is additionally approved for pediatric patients (12+) with obesity and for MASH treatment in adults — indications this packet does not otherwise detail.
Anyone considering Wegovy should discuss the boxed warning and contraindications with a clinician.
uncertainty_notes: Real-world results outside the trial population and duration may differ.

packets.canonical_question: What are the FDA-approved uses, expected results, and major safety warnings for tirzepatide (Zepbound) for weight management?
packets.reader_intent: Gather baseline facts before a clinician conversation about tirzepatide for weight management.
required_limitations: Trial population (SURMOUNT-1) excluded people with diabetes.
SURMOUNT-1's 72-week result does not by itself establish durability beyond the study period.
The thyroid C-cell tumor finding is from rodent studies; the label states human relevance has not been determined.
Weight-change result varies by dose (5/10/15 mg); citing one dose's figure without naming the dose is misleading.
required_safety_context: carries a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodent studies
is contraindicated in people with a personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2
prohibited_claims: cures obesity
guarantees weight loss
produces the same result for every person
has been proven to cause thyroid cancer in humans
approved for cosmetic weight loss with no medical indication required
allowed_conclusions: Zepbound (tirzepatide) is FDA-approved for chronic weight management and, separately, for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in obese adults, and produced substantially greater weight loss than placebo in its pivotal trial.
Anyone considering Zepbound should discuss the boxed warning and contraindications with a clinician.
uncertainty_notes: Real-world results outside the trial population, dose, and duration may differ.

packets.canonical_question: Does eating more protein than the RDA help preserve muscle while losing weight?
packets.reader_intent: Understand whether protein intake above the RDA specifically helps preserve lean mass during a weight-loss effort — not to receive one specific gram-per-day target.
required_limitations: Effect size and the specific protein intake threshold at which the effect is strongest are not reduced to one number applicable to every individual.
prohibited_claims: more protein always builds more muscle regardless of energy balance
the RDA is dangerously insufficient for everyone
eat exactly [X] grams of protein per day to preserve muscle
allowed_conclusions: Protein intake above the RDA is associated with attenuated lean-mass loss during energy restriction, per the cited meta-analysis. This packet does not support stating a specific optimal gram-per-day target or range.
uncertainty_notes: This source addresses energy restriction (catabolic stress) specifically, not energy balance or surplus.

packets.canonical_question: How much water do I actually need to drink each day?
packets.reader_intent: Get a concrete daily water-intake reference number.
required_limitations: Individual water needs vary with climate, activity level, and health status; this is a population-level reference value, not an individualized target.
prohibited_claims: everyone must drink exactly this many liters of plain water per day
this is a medical requirement rather than a population reference value
allowed_conclusions: The National Academies' Adequate Intake figures (3.7 L/day for adult men, 2.7 L/day for adult women ages 19-30, including food) are a reasonable population reference point.

packets.canonical_question: Why does the body seem to resist sustained weight loss, and what does 'metabolic adaptation' actually mean?
packets.reader_intent: Understand why weight regain is common and whether their own metabolism is 'broken.'
required_limitations: Very small sample size (n=14 of 16 original competitors).
Single reality-TV-derived cohort with an unusually extreme initial weight-loss intervention; may not generalize to typical weight-loss approaches.

The raw RMR-below-baseline figure (-704 kcal/day) and the 'metabolic adaptation' residual (-499 kcal/day) are two distinct, separately defined numbers from the same paper and must never be substituted for each other.
prohibited_claims: proves that weight loss permanently and irreversibly damages metabolism for everyone
applies to typical, moderate weight-loss programs
treats -704 and -499 kcal/day as the same figure or as interchangeable
baseline-predicted
predicted from baseline
allowed_conclusions: At six-year follow-up, measured resting metabolic rate was 704 kcal/day below the same participants' measured baseline RMR, per this small long-term cohort.

Separately, the paper's specifically defined 'metabolic adaptation' — the adjusted RMR residual relative to predicted RMR after accounting for 6-year body composition and age — was -499 kcal/day, a real but smaller-magnitude phenomenon than the raw measured-baseline-vs-measured-six-year RMR difference.

Together these show that some degree of metabolic adaptation can persist for years after extreme weight loss — a real phenomenon, but not evidence that every weight-loss attempt causes permanent metabolic damage, and not a single interchangeable number.
uncertainty_notes: Whether and to what degree this generalizes to typical, non-extreme weight-loss programs is not established by this single small cohort.
